findings.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:8 — The category lookup assumes the legacy `embed_category` setting joins to an existing category and immediately dereferences row 0. On fresh/default installations (where no override row exists), or when the configured category was renamed/deleted, the query returns no rows and the migration raises before its intended uncategorized fallback can run.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Backfilled hosts are inserted directly, bypassing `EmbeddableHost`'s scheme/path normalization. Legacy values such as `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234`—formats explicitly exercised by the old tests—will be stored verbatim, while `record_for_host` compares them with `URI#host`; those sites become unauthorized immediately after upgrade.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:13 — Host/category mappings are neither validated as unique nor protected by a unique index, while `record_for_host` selects an unordered `.first`. An admin can create the same host more than once with different categories, after which topic routing is ambiguous and may change with query plans or row churn.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — The model accepts and preserves `host:port`, but `record_for_host` discards the URL port via `URI#host` before comparing. A mapping such as `example.com:8443` can be saved successfully but can never authorize or categorize requests.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — The SQL lowercases only the stored column, not the parsed request host. Ruby's `URI#host` preserves case, so a valid referer such as `https://EXAMPLE.COM/page` fails to match a saved `example.com` entry despite DNS hostnames being case-insensitive.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — The host validator limits alphabetic TLDs to five characters, rejecting valid hosts such as `example.museum` and modern longer TLDs. This makes the new persistence API unable to represent hosts that the prior string setting could accept.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:5 — The normalization callback calls `sub!` on `host` unconditionally. A direct admin API request with a missing/null host raises `NoMethodError` during validation and returns a 500 instead of a validation error.

app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:10 — Update and destroy use `.first` without handling a missing record, then call `save_host(nil)` or `nil.destroy`. Stale IDs produce an unhandled 500 rather than a controlled 404/error response.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:47 — Delete does not attach `popupAjaxError` (unlike save). A failed DELETE leaves the row in place with an unhandled rejected promise and no feedback explaining why the host was not removed.

spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:3 — The new controller specs only assert inheritance; there are no CRUD, authorization, validation, duplicate-host, category-assignment, or not-found examples, and there is no migration/model coverage. Consequently the fatal default-install migration path and the persisted-vs-displayed category mismatch are not exercised by the added tests.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:13 — Host/category mappings are neither validated as unique nor protected by a unique index, while `record_for_host` selects an unordered `.first`. An admin can create the same host more than once with different categories, after which topic routing is ambiguous and may change with query plans or row churn.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. Looking at the diff, the EmbeddableHost model (app/models/embeddable_host.rb) has no uniqueness validation on the 'host' field, and the migration (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb) creates the table without a unique index on 'host'. The record_for_host method uses `.first` without any ordering, meaning if duplicate hosts exist with different categories, the returned record is non-deterministic. This is a real bug where an admin could create duplicate host entries, leading to ambiguous topic routing behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — The model accepts and preserves `host:port`, but `record_for_host` discards the URL port via `URI#host` before comparing. A mapping such as `example.com:8443` can be saved successfully but can never authorize or categorize requests.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. Looking at the diff, the EmbeddableHost model validates hosts with optional port (`:with => /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\/Z/i`) and the before_validation only strips protocol and path, preserving the port. However, in `record_for_host`, it uses `uri.host` which returns only the hostname without port. So if you save 'example.com:8443', the database stores 'example.com:8443', but when checking `record_for_host('http://example.com:8443/page')`, it compares 'example.com' (from uri.host) against 'example.com:8443' in the database, which won't match. This is a real bug where hosts with ports can be saved but never matched.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — The host validator limits alphabetic TLDs to five characters, rejecting valid hosts such as `example.museum` and modern longer TLDs. adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in app/models/embeddable_host.rb line 2 a regex validation: `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i`. The `[a-z]{2,5}` part limits TLDs to 2-5 alphabetic characters. This would reject valid TLDs like `.museum` (6 chars), `.technology` (10 chars), and many other modern gTLDs. The previous implementation using SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts was a simple string list that didn't have this validation restriction, so this is a regression in functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:47 — Delete does not attach `popupAjaxError` (unlike save). A failed DELETE leaves the row in place with an unhandled rejected promise and no feedback explaining why the host was not removed.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in embeddable-host.js.es6, the delete action at line 42-48 shows: `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { this.sendAction('deleteHost', this.get('host')); });` - there is no `.catch(popupAjaxError)` attached, unlike the save action which has `.catch(popupAjaxError)` at line 38. This means if the DELETE request fails, the promise rejection is unhandled and the user gets no feedback about why the deletion failed. This is a real bug - inconsistent error handling where save shows errors but delete silently fails.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new controller specs (spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb) only test inheritance with a single assertion each. The diff shows these specs contain only 'it is a subclass of AdminController' tests. Meanwhile, the controllers (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController and Admin::EmbeddingController) contain actual CRUD operations (create, update, destroy, show) with validation logic, authorization filters, and database operations that have no test coverage. This is a legitimate concern about missing test coverage for newly added nontrivial logic. However, the claim about 'fatal default-install migration path' and 'persisted-vs-displayed category mismatch' cannot be verified as bugs from the diff alone - these are speculative issues.
